hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.1-0.15.
Response has thermal lag with time constant tens to low hundreds of seconds, not instantaneous and no large pure delay.
No large dead zone: small u >0.1 produces measurable heating; dead zone <0.1 if any.
Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with no strong saturation below the soft limit.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior around 0.3-0.7, not at 0 or 1.
Sensor noise is small with short-term fluctuations <0.01, so trends are interpretable.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction and magnitude of gain and lag/time-constant, which determines all subsequent safe step sizes and hold times.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case y = 0.1525 + 0.006*0.5*200 = 0.7525, which stays below soft limit 0.85 with ~0.10 margin.
proposal.expected_observation: If heating hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.15 with short lag then decreasing slope toward ~0.3-0.5, end slope still positive, noise under ~0.01.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero experiments completed, below minimum of 3; gain, lag, decay rate, linearity, steady-state hold input and noise are all unresolved and needed for controller design.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: half power for 200 s to measure heating direction, rate and lag.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Decay at u=0, ambient level, and cooling time constant, which determines passive heat loss, required hold power, and controller integral/drift compensation.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is current y 0.528 + 0.006*0.0*480 = 0.528, well below soft limit 0.85, since u=0 cannot drive heating even with no decay or lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If cooling/decay hypothesis is right, y falls from ~0.53 toward ~0.12-0.16 with falling slope, reaching ~0.2 within ~200s and near flat by ~400s with end slope ~0, plus noise fluctuations ~0.01-0.02.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only E1 completed so readiness requires at least 3 experiments; gain sign and one steady point u=0.5->~0.52 are resolved, but u=0 decay rate and ambient, time constant, linearity/second level, exact hold input for 0.5, dead-zone, and noise level remain unresolved and are needed for safe controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping heater to zero for a long soak to measure natural cooldown, ambient level, and cooling lag.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Second-amplitude steady-state gain and linearity (H5/H6): tests whether 0.25 holds ~0.33 as linear interpolation predicts, to pin down gain and exact power needed for target 0.5.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound from current y=0.137 is 0.137+0.006*0.25*470=0.842, below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9, using conservative no-decay no-lag formula.
proposal.expected_observation: If gain ~0.7-0.8 and tau ~150-200s is right, y rises from ~0.14 toward ~0.32-0.36 with decreasing slope, ~90% settled by ~350s, end slope near 0, with noise fluctuations ~0.02-0.04.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 2 experiments completed, below minimum of 3. Direction, decay to ~0.15, tau ~150s, and u=0.5 holding ~0.52 are resolved, but linearity across levels is untested with only two steady points, precise hold power for 0.5 needs interpolation, and E2 shows noise ~0.02-0.05 larger than assumed, requiring filtering. Not yet sufficient for controller.
proposal.operator_note: Holding low heat to measure mid-range equilibrium and check linearity.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Near-target steady-state gain and exact hold power for y=0.5 given apparent concave nonlinearity between 0.25->0.41 and 0.5->0.52, which sets controller feedforward and gain.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.4152+0.006*0.4*170=0.823 stays below soft limit 0.85, and passive heat loss and short 170s duration keep true level far from hard cutoff 0.9.
proposal.expected_observation: If tau ~150s and concave gain is right, y rises from ~0.41 toward ~0.47-0.49 with decreasing slope, reaching ~0.44-0.46 by 170s with end slope still small positive, noise +/-0.02.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, decay to ~0.155, and tau ~150s are resolved, but linearity is doubted by E4 at 0.41 vs E1 at 0.52 and exact power to hold 0.5 remains 0.35-0.5 with noise ~0.02-0.04, so one near-target step is needed before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping up slightly to 0.4 for a short hold to measure near-target gain without approaching limits.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.12-0.16.
Response has thermal lag with time constant ~80-180s plus small pure delay ~10-25s, not instantaneous.
No large dead zone: u=0.25 produces clear heating from ambient; any dead zone <0.1.
Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with no saturation below soft limit.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior ~0.32-0.40: u=0.25 holds ~0.41 below target, u=0.4 holds ~0.53 above target, u=0.5 holds ~0.52 above target.
Short-term sensor fluctuations/noise are ~0.02-0.04, larger than 0.01 and comparable to band half-width 0.025, requiring filtering/deadband.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Local steady-state gain near target and exact hold power for y=0.5 under apparent saturation (0.25->0.41 vs 0.4->0.53 vs 0.5->0.52), which sets controller feedforward and whether integral must handle concave nonlinearity.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound using current y=0.5328 is 0.5328+0.006*0.32*160=0.8400 below soft limit 0.85, so even with no decay or lag the soft limit cannot be reached and hard cutoff 0.9 is not approached.
proposal.expected_observation: If saturating/concave model with tau ~100-150s is right, y decays from ~0.533 toward ~0.46-0.48, reaching ~0.49-0.50 after 160s with small negative end slope ~-0.0002 and noise +/-0.02; if linear model were right, drop would be larger toward ~0.37.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, decay to ambient, and lag range are resolved well enough for stable tuning, but exact hold power for y=0.5 remains bracketed only between 0.25 and 0.4 with evidence of saturation, and downward local gain near target has not been observed; one small step-down from current 0.53 is needed to pin feedforward and confirm downward controllability before designing controller.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping power down slightly to 0.32 to find the exact setting that holds target temperature.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.12-0.16.
Response has thermal lag with time constant ~150-200s plus small pure delay ~10-25s, not instantaneous.
No large dead zone: u=0.25 produces clear heating from ambient; any dead zone <0.1.
Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with K~1.0; apparent saturation is truncation because short holds are only ~1 tau.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior ~0.32-0.38 centered ~0.34.
Short-term sensor fluctuations/noise are ~0.02-0.04, comparable to band half-width 0.025, requiring filtering/deadband.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives ~30-50% smaller steady rise, but u=0 cooling rate, ambient, delay and sensor unchanged; u~0.38 now holds only ~0.36-0.37.
Change is faster outflow: fall at u=0 is faster and steady level for same u is lower, ambient may be lower.
Change is slower dynamics: pure delay and/or tau noticeably increased, so response to command change starts later and approaches slower.
Change is sensor offset downward ~0.10-0.14 with true thermal dynamics unchanged.
Change is sensor noise/quantization change: increased dropouts, repeats/flat readings, different variance with dynamics unchanged.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Delay from last command change plus u=0 fall rate and ambient, which discriminates faster outflow (faster/lower fall) vs longer delay (later start of fall) vs weaker gain or sensor offset (same fall shape as E2) and reveals sensor noise.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.3567 + 0.006*0*480 = 0.3567, well below soft limit 0.85; margin ~0.49 covers in-transit ~0.39 command even with 60s delay (~0.14 rise).
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-gain hypothesis is right, y holds near 0.35-0.37 for ~20-30s (delay, still responding to prior ~0.39 in transit, possibly tiny rise), then falls monotonically toward ~0.12-0.16, reaching ~0.20 within ~200s and near-flat by ~350-400s with end slope ~0 and noise +/-0.02, matching E2 shape.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, ambient and noise are known from discovery, but gain vs loss vs delay vs sensor offset are confounded in closed-loop after-change trace; a clean u=0 delay/cooling measurement is needed before a gain test, so not ready to generate.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero power to measure delay and cooling rate to separate gain, loss, delay and sensor effects.

proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-gain (~50%) is right, y holds ~0.14 for ~10-20s delay then rises monotonically toward ~0.30-0.36, reaching ~0.27-0.32 by 200s with decreasing slope and small positive end slope, noise +/-0.02 plus occasional -0.03 dropouts; if sensor offset, same shape as E1 but ~0.12 lower; if faster outflow, faster approach to lower steady.
proposal.readiness_justification: E7 confirms u=0 ambient ~0.138 same as before, weakening offset and faster-outflow, and shows immediate fall weakening longer-delay, but post-change heating gain is unmeasured so hold power for 0.5 is unknown; heating step is needed before controller design and budget remains.
proposal.operator_note: Drained to ambient and confirmed u=0 cooling shape; now probing mid-power heat-up to measure new gain.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: High-power steady-state gain and linearity to separate proportional gain loss from fixed sensor offset and faster outflow, which sets new hold power for target 0.5.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.298+0.006*0.8*100=0.778 <0.85 soft limit with ~0.07 margin to soft and ~0.12 to hard cutoff; last change was ~200s ago so ~20s delay cleared and no hidden in-transit rise.
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator (~45% gain, same tau/delay/ambient) is right, y holds ~0.30 for ~15-25s delay then rises monotonically toward ~0.48 steady, reaching ~0.38-0.42 by 100s with decreasing slope and small positive end slope, noise +/-0.02 with occasional -0.03 dropouts as in E8; if sensor offset, rise would be much steeper reaching ~0.55+; if faster outflow, rise would flatten earlier to lower steady.
proposal.readiness_justification: E7+E8 resolved ambient (~0.14 same), delay (~20s same as E1), and noise (dropouts similar to E2/E5), and show ~55% loss of rise at u=0.5 strongly favoring weaker gain, but a single mid-power point cannot separate proportional gain loss from offset or faster-outflow; one high-u linearity check is needed to fix new hold power for 0.5, so not yet ready.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping high from current level to test new gain linearity.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.4131+0.006*0.8*80=0.7971 stays below soft limit 0.85 with ~0.05 margin; same-u continuation adds no new in-transit surge, hard cutoff 0.9 is far, and even +0.03 noise spike stays <0.83.

Ki=0.008 (Ti~81s) trims offset without aggressive windup. Integrate only when |e|<0.15 so initial 0.35 error does not wind up integrator (would add ~0.13 overshoot otherwise). Integral +-0.25 leaves >2x authority over max FF error ~0.11. Filter Tf=15s vs tau 170s smooths 0.02-0.04 noise with negligible lag. U_MAX=0.65 plus yf>0.75/0.80 backstop guarantees steady y<0.82 nominal and forced cooling before 0.85/0.9 even if K=1.2. Rate limit 0.08/s smooths noise chatter.

submission.diagnosis: Same gain, slower dynamics. Evidence: v3 starts at u=0.327 (nominal FF) but y rises slowly (0.117->0.133 in 36s vs E1 0.145->0.186 in 36s at higher u), error stays positive so uff+integral wind to ~0.52 by 150s, y then overshoots to 0.60-0.64 at 300-360s vs v1 0.57, stays high 0.55-0.60 for ~200s, and at 900s slope is still +0.0004 to +0.0008/s with y_mean 0.521-0.525 at u~0.383-0.389 (not settled, 5-tau not reached) whereas v1 slope ~0.0 and settled. Steady-state shift is small (expected 0.547 at u=0.383 with K=1.04, observed 0.521, -0.026) vs large transient prolongation, and zero-input decay test was not run but high-side persistence with low u in v2 (u~0.28 holding y~0.515) indicates retained heat / large tau, not larger leak (which would need more u and decay faster) nor uniformly weaker gain (which would give undershoot, not overshoot). Quantified as tau ~170-180s -> ~260-280s (x1.5-1.6) plus pure delay ~12-15s -> ~28-35s (+15-20s). This produces integral windup overshoot and in_band collapse 0.67->0.25, mae 0.019->0.054.
submission.change_summary: Retuned for ~1.6x slower thermal dynamics: reference time-constant 90s->140s, KP 0.45->0.35, KI 0.010->0.008, KA 0.008->0.004, slow filter 60s->80s, fast filter 18s->15s, U_MAX 0.60->0.65, I limits +-0.20->+-0.25, FF limits 0.12-0.55->0.12-0.60. Structurally gated adaptation: uff/integral frozen for first 60s/30s and unless fast/slow filters agree (|yf-ys|<0.02), plus saturate anti-windup and 0.02/s slew limit kept. This prevents windup during the long lag that caused v3 late overshoot to 0.64 and persistent +0.02 bias, while still learning the higher hold duty needed if gain/loss shifts.
submission.machine_card: Revised assumption: y in [0,1] (0=15C,1=75C), u in [0,1] heater. y_ss = 0.14 + K*u with K~0.95-1.05 (nominal 1.04 from E4: 0.25->0.409). Ambient ~0.11-0.15. Dynamics now: first-order tau ~260-280s (was 150-190s) + pure delay ~28-35s (was 10-25s). Noise ~0.02-0.04 peak requires 12-15s fast + 80s slow filtering and 0.025 deadband. Nominal hold for 0.5 is ~0.34; allow 0.12-0.60 to cover weaker/loss cases. Soft limit 0.85, hard cutoff 0.90 respected via 0.72 cap + 0.78 cut.
submission.design_rationale: Slower plant (larger tau + extra delay) keeps error positive longer; fast integral + fast FF adaptation in v3 wound up to u~0.52 and overshot to 0.60-0.64, then took 200s to unwind (in_band 0.25). Slowing the reference, lowering P/I/A gains and delaying adaptation until settled makes the loop delay-robust (phase margin restored). Widening U_MAX/I_MAX/FF_MAX preserves ability to hold 0.5 if actuator is weaker or loss is larger (needs up to ~0.50), and filtering + deadbands preserve nominal noise performance (band half-width 0.025 vs noise 0.02-0.04). Safety caps at 0.72/0.78 and slew limit prevent hard violations.
